summary: Barbour/Randolph line station: watchman contracted 1913-14, one story and unenclosed in 1916; register says removed by 1997, concrete pad remains.

facts.design: One-story, unenclosed station with a map table under a metal cover (1916 description)
facts.status_note: Removed by 1997; the register describes a concrete pad and shed remnants

events.note: Watchman contracted for three years at Laurel Hill Station (1913-14 state report)
Register says removed prior to 1997 ('By 1997'); no exact date given

evidence.supports: 1913-14 report: watchman contracted for three years at Laurel Hill Station
evidence.quote: L.L. Bennett contracted to supply a watchman at his own expense for a term of three years for Laurel Hill Station.

evidence.supports: 1916: on the line between Barbour and Randolph Counties, seven miles from Elkins
evidence.quote: This station is located on the line between Barbour and Randolph Counties, seven miles from Elkins and five miles from Bellington.
The elevation is 3,075 feet and commands a view of approximately 500 square miles.

evidence.supports: no regular watchman employed; nearby family

notes_for_editor: Build date and builder are not found in any source read (one web search, plus the FFLOS and Eastern pages). Elevation conflict left unresolved: FFLOS 2,927 ft (892 m), kept in the record; the 1916 state report says 3,075 ft. The record's elevation_m (892.1) is not corrected. County: the register says Barbour; the 1916 report puts the station on the Barbour-Randolph line, so no correction is proposed. The 1914 photo already in the record is from the state report; not re-checked. No source describes access or what stands at the site now. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the story's 'sat under a metal cover' wording was not in the source and was rewritten to 'a metal cover was provided against the weather'. The register is now named in full on first use. The removal wording 'by 1997' matches the register's Removed field.
